title: Largest lakes by area
measure: Surface area in square km. All ten figures come from one source, Britannica, so they are measured the same way. Lake areas change with water levels, the Caspian's most of all, so other sources can differ by a few per cent.

entries.name: Caspian Sea
entries.note: Called a sea, but classed as a lake because it's landlocked. Its water level is falling, so its area is shrinking; other sources give 371,000 km².

entries.name: Superior
entries.note: The largest freshwater lake by area.

entries.name: Victoria
entries.note: The largest tropical lake. Some sources give as little as 59,947 km², depending on where swampy margins are counted.

entries.name: Huron
entries.note: Joined to Lake Michigan at the Straits of Mackinac. Counted as one lake, Michigan–Huron would be the largest freshwater lake, at about 117,000 km².

entries.name: Michigan
entries.note: The largest lake entirely within one country.

entries.name: Baikal
entries.note: Seventh by area, but the largest freshwater lake by volume because it's so deep.

entries.name: Great Slave
entries.note: Also the deepest lake in North America.
